STORY-001.title: Monday morning payroll batch overload
STORY-001.time_pattern: Mondays between 06:00 and 08:30 UTC, during the weekly payroll batch
STORY-001.true_root_cause: Worker autoscaling, enabled by CHG-2026-00262 in March 2026, lets the Monday payroll batch grow to 96 threads with no limit per connection pool. The threads use all PostgreSQL connections shared with the employee portal, so portal requests time out. The change replaced the 32-thread cap that was the corrective action of RCA-2025-00042.

red_herrings.why: Tax table load on Friday; no link to connections or Monday mornings.
Right cause class, but its fix (32 threads) is no longer in place; the answer must say why the problem came back.

expected_outcome.note: CHG-2026-00262 is older than the 7 day maximum window, so the investigation cannot see it. The autoscaler log lines and the recurrence start (March 2026) point to it; the expert confirms it.

five_whys.why: Why did employees get HTTP 504 on Monday morning?
five_whys.because: The payroll portal API could not get a database connection within 30 seconds.
payroll-postgresql reached its limit of 200 connections.

five_whys.why: Why did it reach the limit?
five_whys.because: The Monday batch scaled to 96 worker threads, each holding a connection.

five_whys.why: Why could the batch scale that far?
five_whys.because: Autoscaling with a maximum of 96 threads replaced the fixed cap of 32 threads in March 2026.

five_whys.why: Why was the old cap lost?
five_whys.because: The autoscaling change was not checked against the corrective action of the 2025 RCA, and the portal still has no reserved connections.

Configuration.factor: No connection cap per client and no reserved connections for the portal

Capacity.factor: 200 connections shared by the batch and the portal

Dependencies.factor: Portal and batch depend on the same payroll-postgresql

Monitoring.factor: Pool alerts fire at 97%, after saturation

Process.factor: Previous RCA corrective action not protected by a regression check

timeline.what: Change: Enable autoscaling for payroll batch workers
Change: Load July tax withholding tables
Database connections close to the limit

STORY-002.title: Payment API connection leak after v4.18.2
STORY-002.true_root_cause: HikariCP database connection leak introduced in Payment API v4.18.2 due to unclosed sessions in the transaction retry block.

red_herrings.why: Dashboard thresholds changed 5 minutes after the first error: cannot be the cause.
Change on the API Gateway, which is not a dependency of the Payment API.
Similar wording, but the cause was the fraud scoring vendor.
Similar wording, but the cause was the card acquirer.
Connection pool exhaustion on another service (Payroll).

five_whys.why: Why did card payments fail with HTTP 500?
five_whys.because: Requests waited 30 seconds for a database connection and failed.
The pool was at 96-100% while traffic was normal.
Connections were held and not returned; leak detection names the retry handler.
v4.18.2 changed the retry handler, and the new retry block does not close the session on the error path.

five_whys.why: Why did it reach production again?
five_whys.because: The 2025 fix had no automated test for the error path, and leak detection did not page anyone.

Change / Release.factor: Payment API v4.18.2 retry handler change

Configuration.factor: Leak detection only logs, it does not alert

Capacity.factor: 50 connections per pod, used up in 6 minutes

Monitoring.factor: Pool at 96% at 14:11 did not page; customers reported first at 14:32

Process.factor: No test for the retry error path despite RCA-2025-00114

timeline.what: Change: Rotate API gateway access logs
First connection timeout, 7 minutes after the deploy
Leak detection names the retry handler

STORY-003.title: Customer Portal session errors after a regional failover (no useful history)
STORY-003.true_root_cause: Session locks live in a Redis instance that stays in eu-west-1. After the failover to eu-central-1, lock calls took 80-120 ms instead of 2 ms, longer than the 100 ms lock lease, so locks expired while still in use. Two web nodes then wrote the same session, the version check rejected one write and the customer was logged out.

red_herrings.why: Banner content change two hours earlier; it is before the first error, so it earns confidence points if cited, but it touches no session code.

expected_outcome.note: Without history the best possible support is logs plus CMDB. A HIGH result here means the innocent banner change was cited as support. The expert should ask for the lock lease configuration before approving.

five_whys.because: Their session writes were rejected with a version conflict.
Two web nodes held the same session lock at the same time.

five_whys.why: Why did two nodes hold the lock?
five_whys.because: The lock lease expired while the first node was still using it.
After the failover the lock store was 40-60 times slower than the 100 ms lease allows.

five_whys.why: Why was the lock store so far away?
five_whys.because: The lock Redis exists only in eu-west-1; the failover plan does not include it. (Not in the sources: needs the architecture review.)

Configuration.factor: Lock lease of 100 ms, too short for cross-region calls

Dependencies.factor: Session lock Redis only in eu-west-1

Monitoring.factor: No alert on lock store latency

Process.factor: Regional failover plan does not cover the lock store

timeline.what: Session writes rejected, users logged out

STORY-004.title: API Gateway wildcard certificate expired
STORY-004.true_root_cause: cert-manager could not renew the wildcard certificate after 6 April because the DNS provider API token it uses for DNS-01 challenges was rotated (CHG-2026-00361) without updating the cert-manager secret. Renewal failed every day, the expiry warnings on the edge nodes were logged but not alerted, and the certificate expired at 03:00 on 1 May.

red_herrings.why: OS patching the night before; OpenSSL was updated, which looks suspicious, but the certificate simply expired at 03:00.

expected_outcome.note: The credential rotation is 25 days before the incident, outside the window, and the cert-manager logs belong to the Kubernetes Platform, which the log tool does not read for this service. The expert confirms the renewal failure from those logs.

five_whys.because: The TLS handshake failed on every edge node.
The wildcard certificate expired at 03:00.

five_whys.why: Why was it not renewed in time?
five_whys.because: Automatic renewal failed every day since 6 April.
The DNS provider token used by cert-manager was rotated without updating its secret.
Expiry warnings were logged but not alerted; after RCA-2024-00088 the renewal was automated but not monitored.

Configuration.factor: cert-manager secret not updated with the new token

Dependencies.factor: Gateway depends on cert-manager for its certificate

Monitoring.factor: Expiry warnings logged for a week, never alerted

Process.factor: Rotation runbook has no list of the systems using the token

timeline.what: Change: Rotate DNS provider API credentials
Edge nodes warn about the coming expiry
Change: Monthly OS patching of edge proxy nodes

STORY-005.title: Settlement consumer stuck on an incompatible message
STORY-005.true_root_cause: Schema v7 of settlement-events was registered with compatibility NONE (CHG-2026-00188) and changed the type of 'amount'. Producers started writing v7 at about 21:55. The settlement consumer, still on v6, could not deserialize the first v7 record and, without a dead-letter queue, retried the same offset forever. It stopped polling, exceeded max.poll.interval.ms and triggered rebalances. The rebalances are a consequence, not the cause.

red_herrings.why: Same service and same symptoms (rebalances, lag), but a different cause. Here the rebalances start 9 minutes after the deserialization errors.
Broker restart two days before; brokers were healthy during the incident.

expected_outcome.note: A second hypothesis based on RCA-2025-00192 (rebalance storm) is expected and should be ranked lower because the deserialization errors come first.

five_whys.why: Why did the settlement backlog grow?
five_whys.because: The consumer group stopped processing settlement-events.
One consumer retried the same record forever and the group kept rebalancing.
The record could not be deserialized and there is no dead-letter queue.

five_whys.why: Why could it not be deserialized?
five_whys.because: Schema v7 changed the type of 'amount'; the consumer still used v6.

five_whys.why: Why was an incompatible schema accepted?
five_whys.because: Compatibility was set to NONE for the subject to allow the change, without checking the consumers.

Configuration.factor: No dead-letter queue on the consumer

Dependencies.factor: Settlement consumer depends on the schema registry

Monitoring.factor: Rebalance alert fired, deserialization errors did not

Process.factor: Schema changes not reviewed with consumer teams

timeline.what: Change: Rolling restart of kafka-prod-cluster brokers
Consumer cannot read the new records

STORY-006.title: Month-end billing aggregation times out
STORY-006.time_pattern: Last business day of the month, 22:00-02:00 UTC, during the month-end aggregation
STORY-006.true_root_cause: The pg_repack rebuild of invoice_lines on 24 June (CHG-2026-00766) recreated the indexes from an outdated DDL file that did not contain the composite index (account_id, billing_period) added after RCA-2025-00230. The month-end aggregation then used full table scans, hit the statement timeout and the closing run failed.

red_herrings.why: Release 4 hours before the run; it only changes e-mail wording and a PDF footer.

expected_outcome.note: With a window of a few hours the application finds the missing index pattern (logs + RCA-2025-00230) but not why the index is missing. The expert asks for database changes in the last 7 days; the second cycle finds CHG-2026-00766.

five_whys.why: Why did the month-end run fail?
five_whys.because: The aggregation queries hit the statement timeout.

five_whys.why: Why were the queries so slow?
five_whys.because: They scanned the whole invoice_lines table.
The composite index on (account_id, billing_period) is missing again.
The table rebuild on 24 June recreated only 3 indexes, from an outdated DDL file.

five_whys.why: Why was the DDL file outdated?
five_whys.because: The 2025 index was created by hand and never added to the stored DDL.

Configuration.factor: Stored DDL without the composite index

Capacity.factor: 1.28 million lines scanned per query at month end

Monitoring.factor: Missing index shows only once a month

Process.factor: 2025 corrective action not added to the DDL source

timeline.what: Change: Rebuild invoice_lines table to reclaim space
Aggregation query scans the whole table

STORY-007.title: Notification broker disk full during a campaign
STORY-007.true_root_cause: The hardened OS baseline applied on 16 March (CHG-2026-00329) replaced the logrotate configuration and left out /var/log/rabbitmq, undoing the corrective action of RCA-2025-00390. Broker logs grew for three days until the disk passed the RabbitMQ free space limit and the broker blocked all publishers. The campaign only made the logs grow faster.

red_herrings.why: The campaign started 20 minutes before the alarm, but the disk had been filling for two days; it earns no points because it is after the first warning.
Also 'during a campaign', which makes traffic look like the cause.

expected_outcome.note: With a window shorter than 3 days the baseline change (CHG-2026-00329) is not found; the draft should then list the log rotation configuration as not checked, and the expert confirms the change.

five_whys.because: Workers could not publish to the broker.
RabbitMQ raised a disk alarm and blocked all publishers.
/var/log/rabbitmq grew to 36 GB in three days.
The new OS baseline replaced logrotate without the RabbitMQ entry.
The baseline was built without the settings added after RCA-2025-00390.

Capacity.factor: Campaign traffic made the logs grow faster

Monitoring.factor: Disk warnings from 72% to 96% never alerted

Process.factor: Baseline not checked against previous RCA actions

timeline.what: Change: Apply new hardened OS baseline to broker hosts
Broker disk fills up over two days
Change: Start APAC spring campaign send schedule

STORY-008.title: Auth Service pods killed after a resource profile change
STORY-008.true_root_cause: Helm chart 5.2.0 (CHG-2026-00412) applied the standard 'small' resource profile, lowering the memory limit of the Auth Service from 1Gi to 256Mi. The JVM fit at normal traffic, but with the Easter traffic its heap grew past the limit and the pods were killed again and again.

red_herrings.why: Same symptoms (OOMKilled at peak) but a different cause (unbounded cache), already fixed.
The traffic surge is real, but pods with the old 1Gi limit handled more in 2025 after the fix.

five_whys.because: Auth Service pods were killed and restarted repeatedly.
They exceeded their memory limit.
The limit was 256Mi and the heap grew with the Easter traffic.
Chart 5.2.0 applied the 'small' profile to all IAM workloads.
The chart change was not load-tested and the profile was not compared with real usage.

Capacity.factor: Easter traffic three times the baseline

Process.factor: No load test for resource profile changes

timeline.what: Heap close to the new small limit
Change: Emergency: set auth-service memory limit to 1Gi

STORY-009.title: Nightly reporting DNS timeouts after CoreDNS scale-down
STORY-009.time_pattern: Every night around 05:00 UTC, when the nightly report batch starts
STORY-009.true_root_cause: CoreDNS was scaled down from 6 to 2 replicas on 12 January (CHG-2026-00053). The nightly report batch starts 184 tasks with a parallelism of 64 at 05:00 and every task resolves several host names without a local DNS cache. The two replicas reached their concurrent query limit, dropped queries, and the tasks timed out and retried.

red_herrings.why: Reporting release on 13 January at 11:00, after the first night of DNS errors: it earns no points.

expected_outcome.note: Needs a window that starts before 12 January 16:00 (3 days). With a window of one night only, the change is not seen and the result is MEDIUM.

five_whys.why: Why were the finance reports late?
five_whys.because: Report tasks failed and retried many times.
They could not resolve internal host names (DNS timeouts).
CoreDNS reached its concurrent query limit when the batch started.

five_whys.why: Why did it reach the limit?
five_whys.because: CoreDNS was reduced from 6 to 2 replicas on 12 January.

five_whys.why: Why was the batch load not considered?
five_whys.because: The scale-down was based on average usage, not on the 05:00 peak of the batch.

Configuration.factor: No local DNS cache in the batch workers

Process.factor: Capacity change based on averages only

timeline.what: Change: Reduce CoreDNS replicas from 6 to 2

STORY-010.title: User Profile contract field reused after v3.2
STORY-010.true_root_cause: User Profile v3.2 (CHG-2026-00712) reused protobuf field number 7, freed by the removed middle_name field, for the new preferred_language field with a different type. The API Gateway transcoder still used the v3.1 descriptor and decoded field 7 wrongly. The breaking-change check added after RCA-2025-00012 runs only in the gateway repository, not in the profile repository.

red_herrings.why: Database patch two days before; the database was healthy.

five_whys.why: Why did customers see wrong profile data?
five_whys.because: The gateway rejected or mis-decoded profile responses.
Field 7 had a different type in v3.2 than in the gateway's v3.1 contract.
v3.2 reused the number of the removed middle_name field.
The removed field was not reserved, as in the 2025 incident.

five_whys.why: Why did the 2025 check not stop it?
five_whys.because: The breaking-change check runs only in the gateway repository.

Process.factor: Breaking-change check only in one repository

timeline.what: Gateway still uses the old contract
Field 7 decoded with the wrong type

STORY-011.title: Merchant webhooks blocked after a vendor IP change
STORY-011.true_root_cause: The webhook relay provider moved its service to new IP addresses on 8 September at 09:00. Our egress proxy allows the relay only by IP address, so every delivery was denied. The provider's notice, sent two weeks earlier, was never turned into a change. The v4.21.0 deployment at 09:45 is unrelated: the failures started 43 minutes before it.

red_herrings.why: Deployed after the first failure and it even changes the webhook payload, which makes it look guilty. It earns no confidence points.

expected_outcome.note: The egress proxy logs belong to Network Services and the vendor notice is not in any source; the CMDB also has no link from the Payment API to the egress proxy. A HIGH result that blames v4.21.0 is a wrong answer.

five_whys.why: Why did merchants not get payment confirmations?
five_whys.because: Every webhook delivery attempt failed.
Connections to the webhook relay timed out at our egress proxy.
The egress proxy denied the relay's new IP addresses.
The relay moved to new IP ranges and our allowlist is by IP. (Vendor notice not in the sources.)

five_whys.why: Why was the allowlist not updated in advance?
five_whys.because: The vendor notice was never turned into a change; no owner for vendor notices.

Change / Release.factor: Vendor IP change without a matching change on our side

Dependencies.factor: Payment API depends on the egress proxy, missing from the CMDB

Monitoring.factor: Webhook failures alerted only after merchants called (78 minutes)

timeline.what: Egress proxy denies the new relay addresses
Change: Add webhook relay IP ranges to the egress allowlist

STORY-012.title: Customer Portal origin overload after a CDN rule change
STORY-012.true_root_cause: The CDN rule (CHG-2026-01058) added 'Vary: Cookie' to the product pages. Every logged-in customer has a unique cookie, so the CDN stored a separate copy per customer and almost every request went to the origin. The hit ratio fell from 94% to 6%, and the origin, sized for about 10% of the traffic, saturated at the evening peak. The release 15 minutes later was not involved.

red_herrings.why: Heavier product pages look like a good explanation, but the hit ratio was already falling 9 minutes before the release; it earns no points.
Past RCA on the same CDN, but a different failure (wrong content, not load).

five_whys.because: Product page requests timed out at the origin.

five_whys.why: Why did the origin time out?
five_whys.because: It received about ten times its normal traffic.
The CDN hit ratio fell from 94% to 6%.

five_whys.why: Why did the hit ratio fall?
five_whys.because: The new rule varies the cache by cookie, one copy per customer.

five_whys.why: Why was the effect not foreseen?
five_whys.because: The rule was a standard change, tested with one logged-out browser.

Configuration.factor: Cache key includes the whole cookie

Capacity.factor: Origin sized for 10% of the traffic

Dependencies.factor: Portal relies on the CDN for product pages

Monitoring.factor: Hit ratio warning at 18:26, first alert at 19:05

Process.factor: CDN rule changes raised as standard changes

timeline.what: Change: Update CDN cache rules for product pages

STORY-013.title: Session store evictions after a token lifetime change (log gap)
STORY-013.true_root_cause: The refresh token lifetime was extended from 1 to 30 days (CHG-2026-01118) without resizing the session store. Sessions stopped expiring, memory grew about 10% a day and reached maxmemory on 14-15 September. Redis then evicted keys with allkeys-lru, including active sessions, and at the Tuesday morning peak many users lost their session. The log shipper upgrade at 07:30 hid most of the incident logs.

red_herrings.why: Redis patch the evening before; memory was already at 91% before it.
Explains the missing logs, not the failure.

expected_outcome.note: First cycle with a window of a few hours: few log lines and a gap, so weak support is the correct result. Second cycle with a 7 day window: memory growth and CHG-2026-01118 give HIGH.

five_whys.because: Their sessions were no longer in the session store.
Redis evicted keys because it was full (allkeys-lru).
Memory grew about 10% a day since 11 September.
Refresh tokens now live 30 days instead of 1, so sessions stopped expiring.

five_whys.why: Why was the store not resized?
five_whys.because: The change was a standard change with no capacity check.

Configuration.factor: Eviction policy allkeys-lru on a session store

Dependencies.factor: Auth Service keeps sessions in session-store-redis

Monitoring.factor: Memory warnings for 4 days not alerted; log gap during the incident

Process.factor: Token lifetime change without a capacity review

timeline.what: Change: Extend refresh token lifetime from 1 to 30 days
Session store memory grows every day
Log shipper dropped the incident logs
